cohort: The study included 29 late preterm newborn infants followed longitudinally and 88 term infants for comparison at birth.
finding: Late preterm infants showed a gradual progression of motor development until their term-corrected age, with no significant differences in motor evaluations compared to term infants at an equivalent age.
followup_time: Until term-corrected age (approximately 40 weeks post-menstrual age)
cross-section timing: Term infants were evaluated at birth.
gest_age: Late preterm infants (34-35 weeks gestation) and term infants (at least 37 weeks gestation)
